Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y+5z &=5 \\ -x+4y-3z &=-5 \\ 6y+12z &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 5 & 5 \\ -1 & 4 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 6 & 12 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 5 & 5 \\ -1 & 4 & -3 & -5 \\ 0 & 6 & 12 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 12 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 11 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4x-11y+5z &=1 \\ x-3y+2z &=-1 \\ -3x+9y-6z &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -11 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}4 & -11 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -11 & 5 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ -3 & 9 & -6 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & -7 & 14 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z &=-24 \\ x+y+z &=-40 \\ -4x-8y-4z &=96\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & -40 \\ -4 & -8 & -4 & 96\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & -40 \\ -4 & -8 & -4 & 96\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -16 \\ -4 & -8 & -4 & 96\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -16 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 & -24 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & -56 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z &=-12 \\ x+2y-2z &=0 \\ -2x+2y-2z &=24\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & 24\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & 24\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 12 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & 24\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$
